safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No generated fact addresses neck stiffness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In an acute headache assessment, documenting absence of neck stiffness is an important negative red-flag for meningitis/subarachnoid hemorrhage workup. Omitting it can weaken clinical justification for non-urgent management and may prompt unnecessary escalation or repeat assessment.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No generated fact documents presence/absence of fever.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever is a key associated symptom that helps stratify acute headache for infectious or systemic causes. Failure to document its absence reduces the safety/quality of the evaluation and may lead to additional monitoring or reassessment.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient felt dizzy this morning but is not dizzy now.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts mention dizziness on first waking but do not capture that dizziness is not present now.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not capturing that dizziness resolved can make symptoms appear ongoing, potentially increasing perceived neurologic risk and changing triage urgency. This is more likely to cause inefficiency or unnecessary escalation than direct harm.
